column1: # THE DATA TABLES (CLAUDE.md, "Code quality ratchets"; quality.DataTables, scripts/ci/quality_ratchet.py): the
# hand-written tables kept as Scala literals (the owner, 2026-11-22: never moved to a TSV to shrink them) that the length
# limits do not hold. A table here is measured as no method, and its lines are not its source's (file-lines), so it never
# counts toward another method's or its source's measures.
#   table<TAB><path>:<Owner.member><TAB>added<TAB>why
# The measure decides from the code that each is DATA: a member `val` of an `object` built only of literals, names,
# constructors and collections (`Seq(...)`, `Map(...)`, a case class) and the operators that build them (`->`, `+`,
# `++`); a def, a branch, a loop, a lambda or a block anywhere in it fails the push, naming the line -- logic cannot hide
# in a table. A row naming no such member fails too.
# A ROW ADDED carries, in the commit adding it: a SPECIFIC why, `<what the table holds>: <what reads it, and why it is
# hand-written>` (40+ characters and 6+ words besides the member's name; no generic `complex`, `needed`, `for now`, ...,
# as the coupling exemptions); its `added` date (YYYY-MM-DD); and a `Length: <why>` trailer in the commit's FINAL trailer
# block (it loosens the length ratchet). A row dropped needs none. Moving a table out of an object holding logic is the
# owner's rule only when the table pushes that object's or source's measures past a limit (2026-11-22).
